# IBEx.Fi Integration Widget — Full AI Prompt

> Give this document to any AI assistant to build a complete IBEx.Fi
> passkey authentication demo widget. The AI chooses the tech stack.

---

## OBJECTIVE

Build a self-contained web widget that demonstrates IBEx.Fi integration:

1. **One-button passkey auth** — try sign-in, fall back to sign-up automatically
2. **Profile display** — fetch and display user data from `/users/me`
3. **Data update** — write arbitrary key/value pairs to `/users/me`
4. **Token refresh** — keep JWT session alive without re-authentication
5. **Scoped local storage** — cache user data with `${externalUserId}_${key}` prefix
6. **Event log** — real-time display of all API calls, results, and errors
7. **SEPA flows** — support IBAN add/list, payment intent/confirmation, transaction read, and mandate lifecycle

---

## IBEX API CONTRACT

Base URL is configured via environment variable `IBEX_API_URL`.
Example: `https://passkeys-testnet.ibex.fi`

### Endpoints

| Operation | Method | Path | Auth required |
|-----------|--------|------|---------------|
| Sign-in options | GET | `/v1.2/auth/sign-in?wallet=passkeys&rpId=<rpId>` | No |
| Sign-in complete | POST | `/v1.2/auth/sign-in` | No |
| Sign-up options | GET | `/v1.2/auth/sign-up?wallet=passkeys&rpId=<rpId>` | No |
| Sign-up complete | POST | `/v1.2/auth/sign-up` | No |
| Refresh token | POST | `/v1.2/auth/refresh` | No (uses refresh_token in body) |
| Read user data | GET | `/v1.2/users/me` | Yes |
| Write user data | POST | `/v1.2/users/me` | Yes |
| Create address book entry | POST | `/v1.2/users/me/addressbook` | Yes |
| Add IBAN | POST | `/v1.2/sepa/iban/add` | Yes |
| List IBANs | GET | `/v1.2/sepa/iban` | Yes |
| Create payment intent | POST | `/v1.2/sepa/payments` | Yes |
| Confirm payment | PUT | `/v1.2/sepa/payments` | Yes |
| List SEPA transactions | GET | `/v1.2/sepa/transactions` | Yes |
| Get SEPA transaction | GET | `/v1.2/sepa/transactions/:id` | Yes |
| Create mandate | POST | `/v1.2/sepa/mandates` | Yes |
| List mandates | GET | `/v1.2/sepa/mandates` | Yes |
| Get mandate | GET | `/v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id` | Yes |
| Update mandate status | PATCH | `/v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id/status` | Yes |
| Cancel mandate | POST | `/v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id/cancel` | Yes |

`POST /v1.2/auth/sign-in` can return an enriched payload when supported by backend flags (for example `includeBalance`, `includeTransactions`, `includeUserdata`). Prefer this at login to reduce immediate extra HTTP reads.

### Required Headers

**All requests:**
- `X-Rp-Id: <rpId>` — send both `X-Rp-Id` and `X-RpId` variants

**Authenticated requests (`/users/me`):**
- `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`
- `X-IBEx-Auth: Bearer <access_token>` — send BOTH headers

**POST requests:**
- `Content-Type: application/json`

### rpId Resolution

- `*.ibex.fi` or `ibex.fi` → `ibex.fi`
- Any other domain → use hostname as-is
- localhost → `localhost`

---

## AUTHENTICATION FLOW

```
authenticate():
    rpId = resolveRpId(hostname)

    // Step 1: Try sign-in (expected to fail for new users)
    try:
        opts = GET /v1.2/auth/sign-in?wallet=passkeys&rpId={rpId}
        webauthnOpts = decodeBase64UrlFields(opts.credentialRequestOptions)
        assertion = navigator.credentials.get({ publicKey: webauthnOpts })
        result = POST /v1.2/auth/sign-in { credential: encodeAssertion(assertion) }
        tokens = extractTokens(result)

    // Step 2: Fallback to sign-up
    if no tokens:
        opts = GET /v1.2/auth/sign-up?wallet=passkeys&rpId={rpId}
        webauthnOpts = decodeBase64UrlFields(opts.credentialRequestOptions)
        attestation = navigator.credentials.create({ publicKey: webauthnOpts })
        result = POST /v1.2/auth/sign-up { credential: encodeAttestation(attestation) }
        tokens = extractTokens(result)

    // Step 3: Commit session atomically — do NOT call /auth/refresh here
    save(tokens.access_token, tokens.refresh_token)
    save(rpId)
    setHttpAuthContext(access_token=tokens.access_token, rpId=rpId)

    // Step 4: Only now start protected bootstrap calls
    profile = GET /v1.2/users/me (with auth headers)
    save(profile.externalUserId)
    for each (key, value) in profile.data:
        localStorage[externalUserId + "_" + key] = value
```

Bootstrap rule:
- Do not fire parallel `/users/me*` calls before session commit (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, `rpId`, auth-header context) is complete.

---

## WEBAUTHN DATA CONVERSION

IBEx sends binary fields as **base64url strings**. Browser WebAuthn API requires **ArrayBuffer**.

### Decode BEFORE calling WebAuthn (base64url → ArrayBuffer):

**Sign-in:** `challenge`, `allowCredentials[].id`

**Sign-up:** `challenge`, `user.id`, `excludeCredentials[].id`,
`extensions.prf.eval.first`, `extensions.prf.eval.second`,
`extensions.prf.evalByCredential.*` values

### Encode AFTER WebAuthn returns (ArrayBuffer → base64url):

**Assertion (sign-in):** `rawId`, `response.authenticatorData`,
`response.clientDataJSON`, `response.signature`, `response.userHandle`

**Attestation (sign-up):** `rawId`, `response.attestationObject`,
`response.clientDataJSON`

### base64url codec

```
encode: btoa(binary).replace('+','−').replace('/','_').replace(/=+$/,'')
decode: atob(input.replace('−','+').replace('_','/') + padding)
```

---

## API PAYLOADS

### Sign-in options response

```json
{
  "credentialRequestOptions": {
    "challenge": "<base64url>",
    "rpId": "<rpId>",
    "timeout": 60000,
    "userVerification": "required",
    "allowCredentials": []
  }
}
```

### Sign-up options response

```json
{
  "credentialRequestOptions": {
    "challenge": "<base64url>",
    "rp": { "id": "<rpId>", "name": "<rpId>" },
    "user": { "id": "<base64url>", "name": "...", "displayName": "..." },
    "pubKeyCredParams": [{ "type": "public-key", "alg": -7 }],
    "attestation": "none",
    "excludeCredentials": [],
    "timeout": 60000,
    "extensions": {
      "prf": { "eval": { "first": "<base64url>", "second": "<base64url>" } }
    }
  }
}
```

### Sign-in/sign-up completion response (JWT)

```json
{
  "access_token": "<jwt>",
  "refresh_token": "<jwt>",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600
}
```

### Refresh request body

```json
{ "refresh_token": "<current_refresh_token>" }
```

### GET /users/me response

```json
{
  "externalUserId": "<uuid>",
  "subject": "<uuid>",
  "data": { "key": "value" }
}
```

Note: user data may appear under `data`, `userdata`, or as flat root object. Normalize accordingly.
User ID may appear as `externalUserId`, `subject`, `sub`, or `id`.

### POST /users/me request body

```json
{ "data": { "key": "value" } }
```

To delete: `{ "data": { "key": null } }`

### POST /users/me/addressbook request body (important)

```json
{
  "name": "Alice",
  "label": "Friend",
  "userValidated": true,
  "crypto": [{ "chainId": 42161, "address": "0xabc..." }],
  "iban": "FR7616748000011234037943644",
  "respondingPspBic": "AGRIFRPPXXX",
  "remittanceInfo": "Invoice 2026-001"
}
```

Rules:
- `iban` and `respondingPspBic` must be provided together for IBAN creation flow.
- There is no separate client-side VoP endpoint to call here.
- VoP is handled internally by `POST /v1.2/users/me/addressbook`.
- If demo/test seed is required, reuse only the canonical `FAUCET_*` keys defined in `AGENTS.md` (do not duplicate literal values here).

### POST /v1.2/sepa/payments request body (payment intent)

```json
{
  "reference": "PAY-2026-001",
  "channel": "SEPAINSTANT",
  "amount": "150.00",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "remittanceInfo": "Invoice 2026-001",
  "debtor": { "name": "Alice", "iban": "FR76..." },
  "creditor": { "name": "Bob", "iban": "FR76..." }
}
```

Response contains an approval intent (`approvalId`, `approvalHash`, `expiresAt`, `credentialRequestOptions`).

### PUT /v1.2/sepa/payments request body (payment confirmation)

```json
{
  "approvalId": "<approval-id>",
  "credential": {
    "id": "...",
    "rawId": "...",
    "type": "public-key",
    "response": {
      "authenticatorData": "...",
      "clientDataJSON": "...",
      "signature": "...",
      "userHandle": null
    },
    "clientExtensionResults": {}
  }
}
```

### GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions query

- `iban`, `type`, `status`, `statusCode`, `search`, `page`, `limit`.

### POST /v1.2/sepa/mandates request body (summary)

```json
{
  "sourceIban": "FR76...",
  "destinationIban": "FR76...",
  "destinationName": "Bob",
  "destinationBic": "AGRIFRPPXXX",
  "percent": 25,
  "trigger": { "mode": "all" },
  "signature": {
    "message": "IBEX_SEPA_MANDATE_V1 ...",
    "signature": "0x...",
    "safeOperationUserOpHash": "0x..."
  }
}
```

Mandate status transitions are controlled through:
- `PATCH /v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id/status` with `status = validated | suspended | cancelled`
- `POST /v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id/cancel` as convenience cancellation endpoint.

---

## SESSION MANAGEMENT

### Storage keys

- `access_token` — JWT for authenticated requests
- `refresh_token` — JWT for session renewal
- `external_user_id` — UUID from /users/me

### Scoped data cache

User data from `/users/me` is cached locally with prefix:
`${externalUserId}_${key} = value`

### Refresh strategy

1. On sign-in/sign-up success, persist both tokens and use the access token immediately.
2. Access token is typically valid for `expires_in = 3600` (about 1 hour).
3. On 401/403 from authenticated endpoints, run exactly one refresh attempt then retry once.
4. Implement a single-flight/global refresh lock: concurrent 401s must await one refresh, not trigger multiple refresh calls in parallel.
5. Never retry refresh recursively (do not refresh the refresh endpoint itself).
6. If refresh fails (401/403), clear session + scoped cache and transition to disconnected state.
7. Prefer cache-first UI refresh from scoped local storage (`${externalUserId}_*`), then merge network/WS updates.

### Session cleanup

Clear in this order:
1. All entries matching `${externalUserId}_*`
2. `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `external_user_id`

---

## CORS — PROXY REQUIRED

Browser-to-IBEx requests are blocked by CORS (the `Authorization` header is rejected
in the preflight response). Any implementation MUST include a server-side proxy:

1. Browser calls local same-origin routes (e.g. `/api/ibex/*`)
2. Proxy maps to upstream `/v1.2/*` paths and forwards the request server-side
3. Browser sends `X-IBEx-Auth` → proxy adds/maps to `Authorization`
4. No CORS issues since browser only talks to its own origin

### Proxy route mapping

| Local route | Upstream |
|-------------|----------|
| `GET /api/ibex/auth/sign-in/options` | `GET /v1.2/auth/sign-in` |
| `POST /api/ibex/auth/sign-in/complete` | `POST /v1.2/auth/sign-in` |
| `GET /api/ibex/auth/sign-up/options` | `GET /v1.2/auth/sign-up` |
| `POST /api/ibex/auth/sign-up/complete` | `POST /v1.2/auth/sign-up` |
| `POST /api/ibex/auth/refresh` | `POST /v1.2/auth/refresh` |
| `GET /api/ibex/users/me` | `GET /v1.2/users/me` |
| `POST /api/ibex/users/me` | `POST /v1.2/users/me` |
| `POST /api/ibex/sepa/iban/add` | `POST /v1.2/sepa/iban/add` |
| `GET /api/ibex/sepa/iban` | `GET /v1.2/sepa/iban` |
| `POST /api/ibex/sepa/payments` | `POST /v1.2/sepa/payments` |
| `PUT /api/ibex/sepa/payments` | `PUT /v1.2/sepa/payments` |
| `GET /api/ibex/sepa/transactions` | `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions` |
| `GET /api/ibex/sepa/transactions/:id` | `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions/:id` |
| `POST /api/ibex/sepa/mandates` | `POST /v1.2/sepa/mandates` |
| `GET /api/ibex/sepa/mandates` | `GET /v1.2/sepa/mandates` |
| `GET /api/ibex/sepa/mandates/:id` | `GET /v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id` |
| `PATCH /api/ibex/sepa/mandates/:id/status` | `PATCH /v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id/status` |
| `POST /api/ibex/sepa/mandates/:id/cancel` | `POST /v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id/cancel` |

### Proxy rules

- Forward query strings to upstream
- Forward `X-Rp-Id`, `X-RpId`, `Content-Type` headers
- Convert `X-IBEx-Auth` to `Authorization` (send both to upstream)
- Apply the same rpId/header propagation on refresh route (`POST /v1.2/auth/refresh`) in proxy/session layer
- Strip `content-encoding`, `content-length`, `transfer-encoding` from responses
  (most HTTP clients auto-decompress; forwarding these headers causes decode errors)

## DEVTOOLS TOPUP ENDPOINTS (TEST ONLY)

Use these endpoints only for development/integration roundtrip tests (fund -> user action -> return):

- `POST /api/admin/devtools/sepa/topup`
- `POST /api/admin/devtools/crypto/topup`

Rules:
- These are admin/devtools helpers, not production end-user flows.
- Keep one tenant/rpId scope for the full roundtrip.
- Reuse only canonical `FAUCET_*` keys from `AGENTS.md` (do not duplicate literal faucet values here).

---

## rpId REGISTRATION

The rpId must be registered in **IBEXSAFE** for full functionality:

| rpId status | Auth | GET /users/me | POST /users/me |
|-------------|------|---------------|----------------|
| Registered | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Not registered (e.g. `localhost`) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ 400 |

## UI REQUIREMENTS

The widget should include these panels:

1. **Auth panel** — "Authenticate with Passkey" button, connection status indicator
2. **Profile panel** (visible after auth) — display raw `/users/me` JSON, key/value update form
3. **Session panel** (visible after auth) — show truncated tokens, external user ID, refresh button, scoped localStorage entries
4. **Event log** — scrollable log of all API interactions with timestamps

### Design guidelines

- Premium dark theme with modern aesthetics
- Real-time status updates (connected/disconnected indicator)
- Loading states on buttons during API calls
- Error messages displayed in the event log
- Responsive layout

---

## REALTIME WEBSOCKET (RECOMMENDED FOR INTEGRATIONS)

If the implementation includes realtime behavior, add an authenticated WS client that:

1. connects to `wss://<api-host>/ws` (optionally `?blockchainId=<id>`)
2. sends auth as first message within 30s:
   - `{ "type": "auth", "token": "<JWT>", "clientName": "My App" }`
3. listens to user-scoped updates
4. handles at least:
   - userdata updates
   - balances updates
   - transactions updates
5. handles specific WS close/auth semantics:
   - `4001` auth timeout -> reconnect and authenticate immediately
   - `4002` auth failure/token expired -> refresh once then reconnect
   - `4003` duplicate session -> do not auto-reconnect; close previous session first
6. treats initial WS burst idempotently (`user_data` can be emitted twice; ordering is not strict)
7. supports on-demand requests after auth:
   - `get_balance`
   - `get_transactions` (with optional `params` and `requestId`)
8. avoids reconnect storms (backoff + single reconnect controller)
9. falls back to HTTP (`/v1.2/users/me`, `/v1.2/users/me/balances`, `/v1.2/users/me/transactions`) when WS is unstable
10. when WS is healthy, treats WS as the primary data refresh channel for balances, transactions, KY, and IBAN signals (HTTP becomes fallback/on-demand)

## CHAIN CAPABILITY DISCOVERY

Use `GET /v1.2/chains/` to build feature availability by chain before enabling actions in UI.

- A user may have wallets on chains where certain services are unavailable.
- Do not infer service availability from wallet presence alone.
- Resolve chain context from `/v1.2/users/me`:
  - `chainid.defaultChainId`
  - `chainid.chains[].chainId` and associated wallets
- Then join each user chain id with `/v1.2/chains/` entries (`id`) to get:
  - chain name (`name`)
  - module availability (`modules`)
- Gate actions by chain capabilities from `/v1.2/chains/`, especially:
  - transfer
  - recovery
  - automation
  - multi-sig

Example capability payload:

```json
[
  {
    "id": 100,
    "name": "Gnosis",
    "modules": {
      "billing": true,
      "cowswap": true,
      "recovery": false,
      "automation": false
    }
  }
]
```

Practical rule:
- if `users/me.chainid.chains` contains `chainId = 100` with wallets but `/v1.2/chains/` says `recovery: false`, hide/disable recovery actions for chain 100.

## DATA LOOKUP CHEAT SHEET (HTTP + WS)

Use this section to avoid guessing payload paths.

### A) User IBANs

- HTTP (`GET /v1.2/users/me`) typical path:
  - `ibans.ibans[]` with rows like `{ iban, status }`
- WS snapshot (`type = "user_data"`):
  - `data.ibans.data.ibans[]` (section envelope: `{ status, data }`)
- WS signal events:
  - `type = "user_iban_updated"` with minimal payload (`data.iban = "changed"`) -> trigger refresh/read.

### B) User wallets

- HTTP (`GET /v1.2/users/me`) typical path:
  - `addresses.wallets[]` (or `addresses.data.wallets[]` depending normalizer)
  - rows typically include safe/wallet address and chain linkage.
- WS snapshot (`type = "user_data"`):
  - `data.addresses.data.wallets[]`
- Related WS context:
  - `type = "auth_success"` -> `data.safeAddress` is WS session safe only (not full wallet inventory).
  - `type = "chainid_data"` -> default/supported chain metadata.

### C) Address book entries

- HTTP (`GET /v1.2/users/me`) typical path:
  - `addressbook.data[]` with rows like `{ id, name, crypto, ibans }`
- WS snapshot (`type = "user_data"`):
  - `data.addressbook.data.data[]` in strict section-envelope mode
  - if your normalizer flattens section envelopes, use normalized `addressbook.data[]`.

### D) FIAT + CRYPTO balances

- HTTP (`GET /v1.2/users/me`) typical path:
  - `balances` section (commonly includes `type`, `identifier`, `balance.tokens[]`, etc.)
- WS snapshot/response:
  - `type = "balance_data"` with `data.mode = "initial"` or `"request"`
- WS push updates:
  - `type = "balance_update"` (crypto-oriented update)
  - `type = "fiat_balance_update"` (fiat/IBAN-oriented update)

### E) FIAT + CRYPTO transactions

- HTTP (`GET /v1.2/users/me`) typical path:
  - `transactions` section (commonly includes `type`, `total`, `data[]`)
- WS snapshot/response:
  - `type = "transaction_data"` with `data.mode = "initial"` or `"request"`
- WS push updates:
  - `type = "new_transaction"` (crypto-oriented)
  - `type = "fiat_transaction_update"` (fiat-oriented)

Implementation tip:
- Prefer WS events for incremental refresh when WS is healthy.
- Use HTTP reads as fallback/source-of-truth recovery when WS is unavailable or desynced.

### F) CRYPTO transfers (execution + tracking)

- Create transfer intent/execution through Safe operations (`POST/PUT /v1.2/safes/operations`) with transfer operation types.
- Read transfer history via `GET /v1.2/users/me/transactions` with `scope=crypto` and filters (`walletAddress`, `direction`, `tokenAddress`, `hash`, `page`, `limit`).
- Realtime transfer updates come from `new_transaction` (and related `balance_update`).

### G) SEPA payments (execution + tracking)

- 2-step flow: `POST /v1.2/sepa/payments` (approval intent) then `PUT /v1.2/sepa/payments` (passkey confirmation).
- Payment history/status: `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions` and `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions/:id`.
- Realtime status/balance signals: `fiat_transaction_update` and `fiat_balance_update`.

---

## COMMON PITFALLS

| Problem | Cause | Solution |
|---------|-------|----------|
| CORS blocks requests | Direct browser-to-IBEx | Use server-side proxy |
| `ERR_CONTENT_DECODING_FAILED` | Proxy forwards `content-encoding` but body is already decompressed | Strip encoding headers from proxied responses |
| WebAuthn TypeError on extensions | PRF values are base64url strings, not ArrayBuffer | Decode all PRF values to ArrayBuffer before WebAuthn call |
| 401 on `/users/me` after successful auth | Missing auth headers or wrong header name | Send both `Authorization` AND `X-IBEx-Auth` |
| Repeated 401 on `/auth/refresh` with parallel API calls | Multiple requests trigger refresh concurrently | Add a global refresh lock + one shared in-flight refresh promise |
| 401 immediately after `AUTH_COMPLETE_OK` | Protected calls started before session context commit (token/rpId/header source race) | Commit session atomically first, then start `/users/me*` bootstrap calls |
| 400 `rpId is not valid` on POST `/users/me` | rpId not registered in IBEXSAFE | Register rpId or use a registered one |
| Token appears valid but fails | `wallet=passkeys` query param missing from options request | Always include `?wallet=passkeys&rpId=<rpId>` |
| Stale session on page reload | Old token in storage, no validation | On init, try GET `/users/me`; if 401, clear session |
| 401 on many `/users/me/*` endpoints despite valid auth flow | Missing external user context in app proxy/session layer | Persist `externalUserId` from `/users/me` and propagate it in your own backend session model for all proxied calls (including refresh context) |
| WS reconnect loop with repeated auth failures | Reconnect attempts happen without valid refreshed token | Use one refresh path, then reconnect once with backoff; if still unauthorized, force logout |
| WS `ALREADY_CONNECTED` errors | Multiple concurrent sockets for same `(externalUserId, rpId)` | Maintain one active socket per user/rpId and close old socket on re-login before opening a new one |
| Missing realtime updates after connect | Client expects fixed event order or one-shot `user_data` | Handle initial burst idempotently; do not rely on strict ordering; accept duplicate `user_data` |
| Feature shown on wrong chain | UI assumes wallet presence means service support | Query `/v1.2/chains/` and gate transfer/recovery/automation/multi-sig by chain capability |
| Functions not accessible from HTML | ES module scope isolation | Use event listeners, not inline `onclick` |

---

## CHECKLIST

- [ ] rpId resolves correctly from hostname
- [ ] CORS proxy is set up for all `/v1.2/*` endpoints
- [ ] Sign-in/sign-up options include `?wallet=passkeys&rpId=<rpId>`
- [ ] Both `X-Rp-Id` and `X-RpId` headers sent on all requests
- [ ] base64url ↔ ArrayBuffer conversion for all WebAuthn fields
- [ ] PRF extension values decoded before `navigator.credentials.create()`
- [ ] Both `Authorization` and `X-IBEx-Auth` sent for `/users/me`
- [ ] No refresh after successful auth
- [ ] 401/403 triggers one refresh attempt, then session clear
- [ ] Refresh flow is single-flight (no parallel refresh storms)
- [ ] Refresh endpoint itself never enters refresh-retry loop
- [ ] Scoped localStorage uses `${externalUserId}_` prefix
- [ ] `externalUserId` is persisted and propagated in the app session/proxy context
- [ ] `POST /users/me/addressbook` sends `iban` + `respondingPspBic` together when using IBAN flow
- [ ] No direct client call to a VoP endpoint for address book creation
- [ ] SEPA IBAN routes are implemented (`POST /v1.2/sepa/iban/add`, `GET /v1.2/sepa/iban`)
- [ ] SEPA payment flow is implemented in 2 steps (`POST /v1.2/sepa/payments` then `PUT /v1.2/sepa/payments`)
- [ ] SEPA transaction routes are implemented (`GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions`, `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions/:id`)
- [ ] SEPA mandate routes are implemented (`POST/GET /v1.2/sepa/mandates`, `GET /:id`, `PATCH /:id/status`, `POST /:id/cancel`)
- [ ] WS listener handles userdata/balances/transactions updates when realtime is required
- [ ] WS reconnect uses refresh + backoff, without reconnect storms
- [ ] WS auth is sent as first message (`type: "auth"`) within 30 seconds
- [ ] WS close-code handling includes 4001/4002/4003 specific behavior
- [ ] Only one WS session per `(externalUserId, rpId)` is active at a time
- [ ] Initial WS burst is handled idempotently (duplicate `user_data` tolerated)
- [ ] `GET /v1.2/chains/` is used to gate transfer/recovery/automation/multi-sig per chain
- [ ] UI uses scoped local cache (`${externalUserId}_*`) and incremental refresh strategy
- [ ] UI shows real-time event log of API interactions
